findings.finding: Casting and damage shared a ring vocabulary.
findings.action: B/C use warm airborne release sparks; B reserves its ground ring for damage and C uses body reaction plus impact sparks. A preserves the former design for comparison.

findings.finding: The original hit cross could be occluded at body height.
findings.action: B moves the marker to the floor; C uses camera-facing surface sparks and a victim reaction. Tests cover event-time reconstruction, expiry and damage-only triggering.

findings.finding: Preparation backing appeared abruptly, and melee/ice lacked contrast.
findings.action: Both revisions fade preparation over 0.14s and strengthen melee rim, ice edges and area contrast. Stills do not establish the feel of those transitions.

findings.finding: C makes damage conspicuous but briefly washes out fighter color.
findings.action: Keep B available as the color-preserving alternative. Propose C for local confirmation; owner playback decides whether its style is acceptable.

findings.finding: B rings are subtle; neither treatment identifies every attacker or explains target pursuit.
findings.action: Captions/log findings explain the selected exchange without claiming the visuals solve tactical attribution. No combat changes added.

findings.finding: A reviewer reported health text clipped in some three-panel capture displays.
findings.action: Direct-seek and repeated-step screenshots at four1/1.0s are byte-identical to the retained image. All footer text ranges fit their panels; scrollWidth equals clientWidth. Reopened image showed complete text. Retain the reported observation and evidence of investigation.

findings.finding: One reviewer summary ambiguously attributed the second fireball to red.
findings.action: Reviewer corrected it to blue’s second fireball hitting red; preference and concerns remain unchanged.
